stories.headline: AMD acquires AI memory optimization startup MEXT to ease data center DRAM crunch

key_facts.fact: AMD announced on June 15 the acquisition of MEXT, a startup specializing in AI-driven memory optimization technology for data center infrastructure.
key_facts.excerpt: Acquisition expands the AMD AI portfolio and helps customers with memory optimization technology designed to improve performance, reduce total cost of ownership and accelerate time to deployment. AMD is addressing this challenge by acquiring MEXT, a pioneer in AI-driven memory optimization technology.

key_facts.fact: MEXT has developed AI-powered predictive memory technology that makes flash storage behave more like DRAM, expanding usable memory capacity while reducing infrastructure costs.
key_facts.excerpt: MEXT has developed innovative AI-powered predictive memory technology designed to make flash behave more like DRAM, helping expand usable memory capacity while maintaining performance and efficiency. This approach has the potential to reduce infrastructure costs, improve resource utilization, and help customers more effectively scale general-purpose and AI workloads.

key_facts.fact: Financial terms were not disclosed; analysts characterize the deal as small, but AMD says MEXT's technology will be integrated across its data center portfolio.
key_facts.excerpt: The price of the acquisition was likely small as the terms of the deal were not disclosed, but AMD said the startup's technology can help its customers to enhance system efficiency, lower their operating costs and deploy large-scale AI workloads much more rapidly.

key_facts.fact: Dan McNamara, AMD's senior vice president and general manager of compute and enterprise, said integrating MEXT's tech is part of expanding AMD's full-stack compute and AI offerings.
key_facts.excerpt: Dan McNamara, AMD's senior vice president and general manager of compute and enterprise, said the acquisition expands the company's ability to offer differentiated full-stack compute and AI solutions. 'By integrating Mext's technology across the AMD data center portfolio, we expect to help enterprise customers unlock greater value from their infrastructure investments while accelerating AI deployment,' he added.

key_facts.fact: Memory has become a critical constraint across cloud and enterprise environments as AI models, data analytics, virtualization and HPC workloads grow in complexity.
key_facts.excerpt: By increasing the amount of usable memory available to applications, MEXT's technology aims to improve utilization of existing infrastructure and at the same time reduce needs for expensive DRAM. This approach can potentially lower total cost of ownership for cloud providers and enterprise customers and enable larger workloads to run on existing hardware.

stories.headline: Anthropic senior staff meet Trump officials on Fable/Mythos export controls; no resolution

key_facts.fact: Anthropic's senior tech staff Logan Graham, Dave Orr and Nicholas Carlini met Commerce Department officials in Washington on June 15 to discuss the export-control directive blocking Fable 5 and Mythos 5, with additional meetings scheduled at the CIA and with White House science adviser Michael Kratsios.
key_facts.excerpt: The Commerce Department will meet with Anthropic senior tech staffers Logan Graham, Dave Orr and Nicholas Carlini on Monday, officials told Axios. Meetings are also scheduled with the CIA and White House science advisor Michael Kratsios to work through adhering to that cyber executive order.

key_facts.fact: After the Monday meeting, a person close to the talks said the parties are not yet discussing lifting the restrictions, and Anthropic's spokesperson said both sides are 'working quickly to get this resolved.'
key_facts.excerpt: The parties are not yet discussing lifting the restrictions after Monday's meeting in Washington, according to a person close to the talks. Representatives of Anthropic and President Donald Trump's administration 'are working quickly to get this resolved,' the Anthropic spokesperson said.

key_facts.fact: A White House official told Axios that Amazon CEO Andy Jassy raised concerns to senior Trump officials about security risks in Anthropic's latest models, and a White House source said Anthropic's initial position was 'no, we're not going to do anything, this is not a real issue.'
key_facts.excerpt: Amazon's report raised fresh concerns but Anthropic's 'position at the outset was no, we're not going to do anything, this is not a real issue,' the source familiar with the administration's thinking said.

key_facts.fact: CNBC reported the Commerce directive was issued Friday June 12 at 1:00 p.m. ET by phone and confirmed at 5:30 p.m. ET by formal letter, ordering Anthropic to suspend access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 'by any foreign national, whether inside or outside the United States.'
key_facts.excerpt: The government called Anthropic at 1:00 p.m. ET on Friday and instructed the company to disable Fable 5 and Mythos 5 because of an unspecified national security threat, the person said. Anthropic received a formal letter around 5:30 p.m. ET that required the company to suspend the models.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic announced Fable 5 and Mythos 5 on Tuesday June 9 and had worked with government agencies to test the models pre-release with approval to deploy, per a person familiar with the discussions.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic unveiled Fable 5 and Mythos 5 on Tuesday, just days before it received the export control directive from the government. The company worked with government agencies to test the models ahead of the release and received approval to deploy them, according to a person familiar with the discussions.

stories.headline: Bank of Japan raises rates to 1%, highest since 1995, citing Iran war oil shock

key_facts.fact: BOJ voted 7-1 to raise its short-term policy rate to 1.0% from 0.75%, the highest level since 1995 and first hike since December 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: Japan's central bank on Tuesday raised its policy rate to the highest in over 30 years at 1%... This is the Bank of Japan's first hike since December, when it raised rates to 0.75%, and the first time since 1995 that rates have been raised to 1%.

key_facts.fact: Board member Toichiro Asada, the first member hand-picked by dovish premier Sanae Takaichi, dissented, arguing downside growth risks from the Middle East conflict outweighed inflation risks.
key_facts.excerpt: Toichiro Asada, who joined the board in April as the first member to be hand-picked by dovish premier Sanae Takaichi, dissented on the view downside risks to growth from the Middle East conflict were bigger than inflation risks.

key_facts.fact: BOJ flagged upside inflation risk, citing faster-than-expected pass-through of oil prices into consumer prices, and projected underlying CPI clearly above 2% target.
key_facts.excerpt: The BOJ flagged upside inflation risk, citing faster-than-expected pass-through of oil prices into consumer prices across a wide range of goods, and said underlying CPI is expected to reach its target-consistent level between the second half of fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2027

key_facts.fact: Japan's wholesale inflation spiked to a three-year high of 6.3% in May; yen-based import prices jumped 25.5%.
key_facts.excerpt: Wholesale inflation rose 6.3% year on year in May, the fastest pace in three years, while yen-based import prices jumped 25.5%, adding to the cost burden for companies and households.

key_facts.fact: Nikkei 225 hit a fresh record after the decision; yen briefly firmed before giving back gains as investors took comfort the BOJ avoided a 50bp move.
key_facts.excerpt: The immediate market reaction was relatively contained because investors had largely expected the move. The yen briefly firmed but later gave back much of its gain, while the Nikkei 225 rose to a fresh record as investors took comfort that the BOJ avoided a larger 50-basis-point increase.

key_facts.fact: Japan reportedly spent ¥11.7 trillion ($73.5 billion) on yen intervention in May; yen had touched 160 against the dollar and languished there most of June.
key_facts.excerpt: After reportedly splashing out 11.7 trillion yen ($73.5 billion) on intervention operations in May, the yen weakened again, touching the 160 level against the dollar and languishing at that level for most of June.

stories.headline: DeepSeek closes $7.4B first round at $50B+ valuation via LP run by Liang Wenfeng

key_facts.excerpt: Chinese AI startup DeepSeek has raised more than 50 billion yuan ($7.40 billion) at ‌a valuation exceeding $50 billion in its first funding ‌round, using a structure designed to preserve founder control, the Information ​reported on Tuesday.

key_facts.fact: Investors had to put capital into a limited partnership managed by DeepSeek CEO Liang Wenfeng rather than directly into DeepSeek, with a five-year lock-up and no voting rights.
key_facts.excerpt: The funding required investors to put their capital into a limited partnership managed by DeepSeek CEO Liang Wenfeng rather than into DeepSeek itself, the report ‌said. Investors are subject to ⁠a five-year lock-up and will not have voting rights, the report said.

key_facts.fact: China's National Artificial Intelligence Industry Investment Fund is the sole exception, investing directly in DeepSeek with voting rights and no lock-up.
key_facts.excerpt: China's National Artificial Intelligence Industry Investment Fund ​is the ​only exception, having invested ​directly in DeepSeek and ‌retaining both voting rights and freedom from the lock-up, the Information added.

key_facts.fact: Founder Liang committed 20 billion yuan of his own money to the round; Tencent is considering 10 billion yuan and battery giant CATL is considering 5 billion yuan, which would make them the largest external investors.
key_facts.excerpt: Reuters reported earlier this month that founder Liang had committed 20 billion yuan of his own money in this funding round, adding that tech conglomerate ‌Tencent is considering 10 billion yuan and battery giant CATL is looking ​at 5 billion ​yuan, which would make them the largest external investors.

key_facts.fact: Until this round DeepSeek had taken no external venture capital, funded entirely from the balance sheet of High-Flyer, Liang's quantitative hedge fund.
key_facts.excerpt: DeepSeek had been funded entirely from the balance sheet of High-Flyer, the quantitative hedge fund Liang also founded, and the new round is less an opening of the doors than a carefully managed crack.

stories.headline: DOJ files brief defending xAI's unpermitted gas turbines as vital to US military

key_facts.fact: The Department of Justice intervened on Monday, June 15, in the NAACP lawsuit over xAI's gas turbines, asking the court to dismiss the case alongside xAI and the state of Mississippi.
key_facts.excerpt: The Department of Justice intervened in a lawsuit over xAI's gas turbines on Monday. In a filing, the agency sided with Elon Musk's company. The DOJ, along with xAI and the state of Mississippi, asked the court to dismiss the suit, filed by the NAACP in April.

key_facts.fact: The DOJ filing argues that stopping the turbines 'threatens American national, economic, and energy security' by cutting off power for AI 'that supports the Department of War's military operations.'
key_facts.excerpt: According to WIRED, the DOJ filing argues that stopping the turbines 'threatens American national, economic, and energy security by seeking to shut off the power supply for artificial-intelligence innovation that supports the Department of War's military operations.'

key_facts.fact: A declaration from Cameron Stanley, the DoD's chief digital and AI officer, says Grok's Gov model supports 'vital national security missions,' including recent US strikes against Iran.
key_facts.excerpt: A declaration from Cameron Stanley, the DoD's chief digital and AI officer, states that Grok's Gov model supports 'vital national security missions' including recent U.S. strikes against Iran.

key_facts.fact: The DOJ memorandum states there are only four AI models, including Grok, that 'support mission-critical operations across Secret and Top-Secret classified networks.'
key_facts.excerpt: According to the DOJ memorandum, there are only four artificial intelligence models, including Grok, that 'support mission-critical operations across Secret and Top-Secret classified networks.'

key_facts.fact: The NAACP suit, filed April 14, 2026, alleges xAI is operating unpermitted natural gas turbines at its Colossus 2 data center in Southaven, Mississippi, violating the Clean Air Act and endangering nearby communities.
key_facts.excerpt: The Department of Justice, along with the state of Mississippi, are asking the court to dismiss the lawsuit the NAACP filed against xAI in April. If you'll recall, the organization sued xAI for allegedly operating methane gas turbines to power its Colossus 2 data center in South Memphis without the proper permit. It later asked the court for an injunction to stop xAI from running the turbines, explaining that they increase 'risks of asthma attacks and heart disease.'

stories.headline: FDA approves first PD-1/HIF-2α combo (Keytruda + Welireg) for high-risk kidney cancer

key_facts.fact: The FDA approved Merck's Welireg (belzutifan) in combination with Keytruda (pembrolizumab) as adjuvant treatment for adults with renal cell carcinoma with a clear cell component at intermediate-high or high risk of recurrence after nephrectomy.
key_facts.excerpt: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Merck & Co's (NYSE: MRK) Welireg (belzutifan) in combination with Keytruda (pembrolizumab)... for the adjuvant treatment of adults with renal cell carcinoma (RCC) with a clear cell component at intermediate-high or high risk of recurrence following nephrectomy.

key_facts.fact: Merck said the decision marks the first approval of PD-1 and hypoxia-inducible factor-2 alpha (HIF-2α) inhibitor combination regimens.
key_facts.excerpt: Merck said the decision marks the first approval of PD-1 and hypoxia-inducible factor-2 alpha (HIF-2α) inhibitor combination regimens.

key_facts.fact: Approval is based on the Phase III LITESPARK-022 trial including 1,841 participants, led by Toni Choueiri of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.
key_facts.excerpt: The approval is based on results from the Phase III LITESPARK-022 trial, led by Toni Choueiri, MD, director of the Lank Center for Genitourinary Oncology at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute... The LITESPARK-022 study... included 1,841 participants with ccRCC.

key_facts.fact: With median 28.4-month follow-up, the combination cut the risk of recurrence, metastasis or death by 28%; about 81% on the regimen were cancer-free at 24 months vs 74% on standard-of-care.
key_facts.excerpt: With a median follow-up of 28.4 months, the combination of pembrolizumab plus belzutifan resulted in a 28% decrease in the risk of recurrence, metastasis or death. About 81% of participants who took the two-drug regimen were cancer-free after an estimated 24 months, compared with 74% of those who received the standard-of-care regimen of pembrolizumab plus placebo.

key_facts.fact: FDA also approved the subcutaneous combination of pembrolizumab and berahyaluronidase alfa-pmph (Keytruda Qlex) plus belzutifan.
key_facts.excerpt: The FDA also approved the subcutaneous combination of pembrolizumab and berahyaluronidase alfa-pmph plus belzutifan.

stories.headline: France replaces Palantir at DGSI with ChapsVision; €655M sovereign-AI plan, Mistral assistant for 1M state agents

key_facts.fact: French PM Sébastien Lecornu announced on June 16 that the DGSI domestic intelligence agency is terminating its Palantir contract and migrating to French rival ChapsVision.
key_facts.excerpt: The French domestic intelligence agency DGSI has decided to terminate its contract with the U.S. tech firm Palantir in favour of a French rival, ChapsVision, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said on Tuesday.

key_facts.fact: The Palantir contract had been renewed for three years in December 2025 and was set to run until 2028 before being cut short; ChapsVision was also selected by Germany's BfV in May 2026 for similar work.
key_facts.excerpt: courait jusqu'en 2028... cet accord avait été renouvelé pour trois ans en décembre 2025... Exit donc le géant américain : place à ChapsVision, déjà sélectionnée par Berlin en mai dernier pour assurer des missions similaires au profit du renseignement intérieur allemand, le BfV.

key_facts.fact: France will invest an additional €655 million ($760 million) in AI through the France 2030 program, targeting infrastructure, compute, research and industrial supply chains.
key_facts.excerpt: Lecornu said France plans to invest €655 million ($760 million) in artificial intelligence, and set up a shared chatbot for all state services.

key_facts.fact: France will roll out a sovereign Assistant chatbot powered by Mistral AI to about 1 million state employees (out of 2.6 million), after a 10-month pilot with 10,000 civil servants in Interior, Justice and Bercy; estimated cost is around €700,000.
key_facts.excerpt: Après dix mois d'expérimentation auprès de 10 000 fonctionnaires répartis entre les ministères de l'Intérieur, de la Justice et plusieurs services de Bercy, l'outil sera désormais accessible à environ un million d'agents connectés au réseau interministériel, sur un total de 2,6 millions. Le coût de cette extension : 700 000 euros, incluant l'accès aux modèles de Mistral et aux capacités de calcul.

key_facts.fact: Lecornu framed the moves as a sovereignty bid: 'We must use our own AI models; we cannot accept new strategic dependencies in the digital sphere... France must have its own tools.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'We must use our own AI models; we cannot accept new strategic dependencies in the digital sphere,' Lecornu said in a video posted on X. 'We cannot rely on tools developed by foreign powers. France must have its own tools.'

stories.headline: Google commits $1.5B to expand Alabama data center, pledging to cover power costs

key_facts.fact: Google announced on June 15 that it will spend $1.5 billion across 2026 and 2027 to expand its Jackson County, Alabama data center campus.
key_facts.excerpt: Google announced Monday that it will spend $1.5 billion across 2026 and 2027 to expand its data center campus in Jackson County, Alabama, pairing the buildout with a promise to cover its own power and infrastructure costs.

key_facts.fact: Google said it will pay for 100% of the power it uses and cover infrastructure costs directly driven by the Jackson County expansion, in line with the US Ratepayer Protection Pledge.
key_facts.excerpt: Google says that the entirety of the 'power and infrastructure' will be funded by the company in line with the US government's Ratepayer Protection Pledge. Abiding by that pledge means Google would need to plan so that local electricity costs would not increase as a result of the increased activity in Google's Jackson County data center.

key_facts.fact: The expansion will eventually be powered by advanced nuclear via Google's 2025 partnership with Kairos Power and TVA, supplying up to 50 megawatts of clean power to data centers in Alabama and Tennessee.
key_facts.excerpt: Google notes that the expansion will eventually be powered by nuclear power through a partnership put in place between Google, Kairos, and TVA in 2025. The agreement supplies Google with up to 50 megawatts of clean power to data centers in both Alabama and Tennessee.

key_facts.fact: Google has contracted more than 300 MW of new generation capacity to the Tennessee Valley region; the Kairos Power Hermes 2 SMR is scheduled to begin operations in 2030, with broader 500 MW capacity targeted by 2035.
key_facts.excerpt: Kairos has described Hermes 2 as the first deployment under its broader agreement with Google to bring 500 megawatts of advanced nuclear capacity online by 2035. The company has said Hermes 2 is scheduled to begin operations in 2030, which means it is not the near-term answer for a 2026-2027 data center expansion. For now, the more immediate pieces are the 300-plus megawatts of contracted generation capacity.

key_facts.fact: The campus has operated since 2019 on the site of TVA's retired Widows Creek coal plant in Jackson County, Alabama.
key_facts.excerpt: Google's Alabama campus has operated since 2019 on the site of the Tennessee Valley Authority's retired Widows Creek coal plant.

stories.headline: Nvidia sells $25B in first bond offering since 2021 with $85B in investor demand

key_facts.excerpt: Chipmaking giant Nvidia Corp. sold $25 billion of high-grade bonds, joining a wave of jumbo debt offerings from tech heavyweights as investors clamor to get exposure to the artificial intelligence boom. The deal, priced on Monday, attracted as much as $85 billion of orders or more than three times the size of the bond.

key_facts.fact: Investor demand reached approximately $85 billion, more than three times the size of the bond, and the offering was boosted from an initial target of $20 billion.

stories.headline: OpenAI's audited 2025 financials: $34B in costs on $13B revenue, $38.5B net loss

key_facts.fact: OpenAI spent $34 billion in 2025 on $13 billion in revenue, including $19.18 billion on research and development and $5.73 billion on sales and marketing, per audited financial documents reviewed by the Financial Times.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI spent $34 billion last year to dominate the booming AI market ahead of its planned IPO, the Financial Times reported on Monday. Audited financial figures show the ChatGPT maker spent about $19 billion on research and development in 2025 and nearly $6 billion on sales and marketing, as well as other costs, the report said.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI's 2025 net loss attributable to the company was $38.5 billion, up roughly 8x from a $5.09 billion net loss in 2024.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI lost around $38.5 billion in 2025... Ultimately, the net loss attributable to OpenAI in 2025 was $38.5 billion.

key_facts.fact: The 2025 loss was inflated by a $41.55 billion non-cash charge tied to the fair-value re-mark of convertible interests and warrant liabilities from the for-profit conversion.
key_facts.excerpt: The 2025 losses were heavily influenced by the company's transition from a non-profit to a for-profit structure, which triggered a $41.55 billion loss related to changes in the fair value of convertible interests and warrant liabilities.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI paid Microsoft $17.2 billion in 2025, including $10.59 billion classified as R&D — largely the cost of training OpenAI's models — and received $303 million from Microsoft.
key_facts.excerpt: In the 2025 calendar year, OpenAI paid Microsoft $10.59 billion for 'Research and development' expenses. We believe this most likely refers to the cost of training OpenAI's models... In total, OpenAI's expenses to Microsoft amounted to $17.2 billion.

key_facts.fact: SoftBank paid OpenAI $867 million in 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: In 2025, SoftBank paid OpenAI $867 million. Microsoft paid it $303 million.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI confidentially filed for an IPO with the SEC last week.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI confidentially filed for an IPO with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission last week. The company has not set a public timeline for the offering.

stories.headline: OpenRouter launches Fusion, a multi-model deliberation API matching Fable-5 on deep research

key_facts.fact: OpenRouter launched Fusion, a 'compound model' API that fans a prompt out to a panel of AI models in parallel, has a judge model produce a structured analysis, then a synthesizer writes the final answer.
key_facts.excerpt: When you send a prompt to Fusion, we dispatch it to a panel of models in parallel, each with web search and web fetch enabled. A judge model reads every panel response and produces structured analysis: consensus points, contradictions, partial coverage, unique insights, blind spots. The calling model then writes the final answer grounded in that analysis.

key_facts.fact: On OpenRouter's internal benchmark of 100 hard DRACO deep-research tasks, a Fusion panel of Fable 5 + GPT-5.5 scored ~69%, edging combinations of Opus 4.8 + GPT-5.5 + Gemini 3.1 Pro; solo Claude Fable 5 scored ~65%.
key_facts.excerpt: The headline result: Fable 5 + GPT-5.5 in fusion came in at approximately 69%, edging out Opus 4.8 + GPT-5.5 + Gemini 3.1 Pro and Opus 4.8 + GPT-5.5 combinations. Solo Claude Fable 5 landed around 65%.

key_facts.fact: A budget Fusion panel of Gemini 3 Flash, Kimi K2.6 and DeepSeek V4 Pro outperformed solo GPT-5.5 and solo Claude Opus 4.8 and came within 1% of Fable 5's score at roughly half Fable 5's price.
key_facts.excerpt: A panel of Gemini 3 Flash, Kimi K2.6, and DeepSeek V4 Pro — three models well below frontier pricing — fused together outperformed solo GPT-5.5 and solo Claude Opus 4.8, and came within 1% of Fable 5's score. OpenRouter says that panel costs roughly half what Fable 5 would have.

key_facts.fact: Fusion costs are the sum of all panel + judge completions; with the default 3-model 'Quality' preset (Opus, GPT, Gemini Pro) expect roughly 4–5× the cost of a single completion.
key_facts.excerpt: Fusion runs N panel calls + 1 judge call in addition to your normal request. With the default 3-model panel, expect roughly 4–5× the cost of a single completion on the same prompt. Cost scales linearly with panel size.

key_facts.fact: OpenRouter says roughly three-quarters of Fusion's performance gain comes from the synthesis step, with one-quarter from model diversity.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenRouter says roughly three-quarters of Fusion's performance gain comes from that synthesis step — combining what the models produced — with the remaining quarter coming from the diversity of models themselves.

stories.headline: Qualcomm in talks to buy AI chip startup Tenstorrent for $8B-$10B

key_facts.fact: Qualcomm is in talks to acquire AI chip startup Tenstorrent for between $8 billion and $10 billion, per The Information citing a person with direct knowledge.
key_facts.excerpt: Qualcomm is in talks to acquire AI chip startup Tenstorrent for $8 ‌billion to $10 billion, The Information reported ‌on Monday citing a person with knowledge of the ​deal.

key_facts.fact: Talks are ongoing and the price could change or discussions could fall apart; it is unclear if the price includes performance-based milestone payments.
key_facts.excerpt: The talks were ongoing and the price could change, or the discussions could fall apart, ‌according to the ⁠report. It was not clear if the price will include performance-based milestone ⁠payments, a structure used in the past to buy chip startups, the Information added.

key_facts.fact: Tenstorrent was founded in 2016 and is led by chip designer Jim Keller, a former Apple chip architect who also led Tesla's autonomous-driving chip effort.
key_facts.excerpt: Founded ‌in 2016, Tenstorrent is headed ‌by Jim Keller, a former ​Apple chip ​designer who also oversaw Tesla's efforts to design a chip for autonomous driving. The startup ​develops accelerators ‌for training AI models and running AI ​applications.

key_facts.fact: An $8B-$10B price would be a significant step up from Tenstorrent's last targeted valuation of about $3.2 billion in a roughly $800 million round earlier in the year.
key_facts.excerpt: Just months ago, TechStartups reported that Toronto-founded Tenstorrent was seeking roughly $800 million in funding at a $3.2 billion valuation. A deal near $10 billion would represent a dramatic increase in value in less than a year.

key_facts.fact: Qualcomm shares fell about 1% in extended trading after the report.
key_facts.excerpt: Shares of Qualcomm fell about 1% in extended trading.

stories.headline: French silicon-quantum startup Quobly closes €115M Series A backed by STMicro

key_facts.fact: Quobly announced on June 15 the closing of a €115 million Series A to accelerate the industrialization of its silicon-based quantum computers.
key_facts.excerpt: Quobly has announced the closing of a EUR115 million Series A financing to accelerate the industrialization of its silicon-based quantum computers and bring its first commercial product to market by the end of 2026, the French quantum computing company said.

key_facts.fact: The round is led by Bpifrance, SEALSQ and STMicroelectronics, with participation from the European Innovation Council, Blast, ALIAD (Air Liquide Venture Capital) and Innovacom.
key_facts.excerpt: The round is led by Bpifrance, SEALSQ and STMicroelectronics, with participation from the European Innovation Council (EIC Fund), Blast, ALIAD (Air Liquide Venture Capital) and existing investor Innovacom, bringing together leading industrial, sovereign and deeptech investors.

key_facts.fact: Quobly plans to deploy its first commercial quantum computer through the cloud by the end of 2026 under its Alloy product line.
key_facts.excerpt: The French company, bringing semiconductor-grade manufacturing and industrialization to quantum computing, plans to deploy its first commercial quantum computer through the cloud by the end of 2026 under its Alloy product line.

key_facts.fact: CEO and co-founder Maud Vinet said the company has shown silicon qubits can be developed within semiconductor manufacturing processes and integrated into a system architecture.
key_facts.excerpt: 'Over the past two years, we have demonstrated that silicon qubits can be developed within semiconductor manufacturing processes and integrated into a system architecture,' said Maud Vinet, CEO and co-founder, Quobly. 'With this Series A, we are accelerating the deployment of our first commercial systems and building a quantum computing platform designed to integrate into existing computing infrastructures.'

key_facts.fact: Existing Quobly shareholders include the CEA, CNRS, Quantonation and Supernova Invest.
key_facts.excerpt: Existing shareholders also include the CEA, CNRS, Quantonation and Supernova Invest.

stories.headline: Salesforce to acquire AI customer-service platform Fin (ex-Intercom) for ~$3.6B

key_facts.fact: Salesforce signed a definitive agreement to acquire Fin, formerly Intercom, for approximately $3.6 billion, subject to customary purchase-price adjustments.
key_facts.excerpt: Salesforce will acquire Fin for approximately $3.6 billion, subject to customary purchase price adjustments.

key_facts.fact: Fin's core product is an AI agent powered by its proprietary model, Apex, resolving customer queries across live chat, email, WhatsApp, SMS, phone, and Slack.
key_facts.excerpt: Fin's core offering, its AI Agent, resolves complex customer queries end-to-end, across every channel, including live chat, email, WhatsApp, SMS, phone, and Slack. The AI Agent is powered by the company's proprietary AI model, Apex, that is purpose-built for customer support.

key_facts.fact: Fin says its AI Agent has resolved on average 76% of support volume end-to-end and serves more than 30,000 companies.
key_facts.excerpt: The AI Agent has already demonstrated strong customer outcomes, including examples of AI agents resolving on average 76% of support volume end-to-end. The acquisition will also bring a long-tenured technical AI team and an established global customer base of more than 30,000 companies to Salesforce.

key_facts.fact: The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of Salesforce's fiscal year 2027 and Salesforce will not change its FY27 financial guidance.
key_facts.excerpt: The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of Salesforce's fiscal year 2027, subject to the satisfaction of customary closing conditions, including the receipt of required regulatory clearances.

key_facts.fact: Intercom was founded in 2011 by Eoghan McCabe, Des Traynor, Ciaran Lee and David Barrett and renamed Fin in May 2026; McCabe remains CEO post-deal.
key_facts.excerpt: McCabe started Intercom in 2011, with Des Traynor, Ciaran Lee and David Barrett. The company changed its name to Fin last month, though McCabe said in a blog post at the time that the customer service software would continue as Intercom.

key_facts.fact: Salesforce's largest prior acquisition was the $27+ billion Slack deal that closed in 2021.
key_facts.excerpt: The cloud company's largest acquisition was a more than $27 billion deal for chat software platform Slack

stories.headline: SpaceX flies first Falcon 9 as a public company, deploys 1,500th Starlink of 2026

key_facts.fact: SpaceX launched the Starlink 17-54 mission from Vandenberg Space Force Base at 8:34 a.m. PDT on June 15, deploying 24 Starlink V2 Mini satellites — the first Falcon 9 flight as a publicly traded company.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX marked a historic double milestone on June 15, 2026, executing its first Falcon 9 launch as a publicly traded company just hours after its Nasdaq debut, with booster B1093 lifting off from Vandenberg Space Force Base at 8:34 a.m. PDT and deploying 24 Starlink V2 Mini satellites — including the 1,500th Starlink launched so far this year.

key_facts.fact: Booster B1093 completed its 14th flight and landed on the drone ship 'Of Course I Still Love You', marking SpaceX's 624th booster landing.
key_facts.excerpt: A little more than eight minutes after liftoff, B1093 landed on the drone ship, 'Of Course I Still Love You', positioned in the Pacific Ocean. It was the 203rd landing on this vessel and the 624th booster landing for SpaceX.

key_facts.fact: The launch raised the active Starlink constellation to 10,660 satellites, according to tracker Jonathan McDowell; over 80% of SpaceX's 69 Falcon 9 flights this year have been Starlink missions.
key_facts.excerpt: The satellites (known as Group 17-54) raised the Starlink megaconstellation to 10,660 active units, according to tracker Jonathan McDowell... Monday's launch was SpaceX's 69th Falcon 9 mission of the year. More than 80% of those flights have been Starlink missions.

key_facts.fact: SPCX shares surged 19% on their first full trading day; Ron Baron followed with a $1 billion purchase of SPCX, bringing Baron Capital's total SpaceX holdings to ~$25 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: The stock surged 19% on its first trading day as CEO Elon Musk projected the company could reach $1 trillion in annual revenue by 2030... Renowned fund manager Ron Baron followed the IPO with a $1 billion purchase of SPCX shares, bringing Baron Capital's total SpaceX holdings to an eye-watering $25 billion.

key_facts.fact: SpaceX's Dragon CRS-34 cargo capsule is set to depart the International Space Station on June 16.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX's Dragon CRS-34 cargo capsule is set to depart the International Space Station on June 16, closing out another busy operational week.

stories.headline: Texas governor issues disaster declaration for 101 counties as Houston floods

key_facts.fact: Texas Governor Greg Abbott issued a disaster declaration for 101 counties on June 15, including Harris County, as severe storms and flooding threatened the state.
key_facts.excerpt: Texas Governor Greg Abbott announced Monday that he has issued a disaster declaration for 101 Texas counties as severe storms continue to threaten the state. Harris County is among the counties on the list.

key_facts.fact: Flooding hit Greater Houston on June 15; floodwaters closed parts of Interstate 45, the University of Houston Downtown campus including its food bank, and stranded vehicles under bridges.
key_facts.excerpt: Flooding impacted many parts of the Greater Houston area on Monday... Cars drove through high water throughout the area. Some vehicles became stuck under bridges and had to be towed. The flooding forced closures at the University of Houston Downtown, including its on-campus food bank.

key_facts.fact: Abbott directed the Texas Division of Emergency Management to activate additional resources and implement 24-hour operations at the State Emergency Operations Center.
key_facts.excerpt: Gov. Abbott also directed the Texas Division of Emergency Management (TDEM) to activate additional state emergency response resources and implement 24-hour operations at the Texas State Emergency Operations Center as storm risks persist.

key_facts.fact: Harris County Emergency Management Director Mark Sloan warned residents the danger was 'far from over' with more heavy rain expected overnight into June 16.
key_facts.excerpt: Harris County Emergency Management Director Mark Sloan made clear that the danger is far from over. 'This is not over. We still anticipate some heavy rains with street issues, especially overnight into the morning hours,' Sloan said.

key_facts.fact: Separately in California, the Shore Fire near Calimesa in Riverside County grew to 1,500 acres by 8 p.m. June 15, forcing evacuations and shutting down Highway 60 westbound.
key_facts.excerpt: A brush fire in Riverside County has grown to 1,500 acres and prompted evacuation orders Monday, authorities said... The fire stood at about 1,500 acres as of 8 p.m., according to Cal Fire.

key_facts.fact: In Washington state, the Twin Sisters Fire south of Wallula Junction grew to 8,262 acres by June 15 amid a red flag warning for central and eastern Washington and northeast Oregon.
key_facts.excerpt: The Twin Sisters Fire, located about five miles south of Wallula Junction, grew to 8,262 acres on Monday, June 15... A red flag warning was in effect for much of central and eastern Washington and northeast Oregon Monday morning through Tuesday evening, June 16, for high winds and low relative humidity.

stories.headline: Ukraine drone strike hits Moscow's largest oil refinery, 15 km from the Kremlin

key_facts.fact: Ukrainian drones struck the Moscow Oil Refinery in the Kapotnya district on the morning of June 16, igniting a fire roughly 15 kilometers from the Kremlin and about 500 km from Ukrainian-held territory.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukrainian drones struck the Moscow Oil Refinery in the Kapotnya district on the morning of 16 June, igniting a fire at the plant roughly 15 kilometers from the Kremlin and some 500 kilometers from Ukrainian-held territory.

key_facts.fact: Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said 25 drones were destroyed over the city; one damaged a facility at the Moscow Oil Refinery, with no casualties reported.
key_facts.excerpt: Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin wrote on Telegram on June 16 that 25 drones were 'destroyed' over the city, and that one of them damaged a facility at the Moscow Oil Refinery. He added that there were no casualties and that emergency services were at the site of the attack.

key_facts.fact: Zelensky framed the strike as a 'just response' to Russian attacks and said the SBU, Unmanned Systems Forces, Special Operations Forces and military intelligence (HUR) were involved.
key_facts.excerpt: The Security Service of Ukraine (SBU), the Unmanned Systems Forces, the Special Operations Forces, and Ukraine's military intelligence (HUR) were involved in the operation, Zelensky said... 'This is a just response to Russian strikes – and to the dragging out of a war that must be ended,' Zelensky added.

key_facts.fact: Russia attacked Ukraine overnight with two Iskander-M ballistic missiles and 132 drones from the evening of June 15; Ukrainian air defenses destroyed or jammed 114 of the drones, with hits at nine locations.
key_facts.excerpt: Russian forces attacked Ukraine with two Iskander-M ballistic missiles and 132 drones of various types on the night of 15-16 June. Ukrainian air defence forces have downed 114 UAVs, with strikes recorded at nine locations.

key_facts.fact: The strike hit the refinery's ELOU AVT-6 primary crude-distillation unit, the capital's largest refinery, located inside Russia's densest air-defense belt.
key_facts.excerpt: The Ukrainian monitoring channel Exilenova identified the burning unit as the ELOU AVT-6 — the refinery's primary crude-distillation unit... Kapotnya sits inside the densest air-defense belt in the country.

key_facts.fact: Drone strikes on Russian refineries have doubled since the start of 2026, leading to full or partial shutdowns and a decline in gasoline, diesel and jet fuel production.
key_facts.excerpt: The number of drone strikes on Russian refineries has doubled since the start of 2026, leading to full or partial shutdowns of oil processing and a decline in the production of gasoline, diesel, and jet fuel
